body.claim: Too many similar options can leave people less satisfied, but only under certain conditions.
body.why: With many equally good options, each must be weighed against the others. Satisfaction is described by an inverted U: it rises, peaks, then falls into pressure and confusion. The effect is not universal. It needs a chooser with no clear prior preference and no clearly dominant option. With a preference, the number of options has little impact.

probes.question: Which situation is most likely to cause choice overload?
options: Many equally good options and no clear preference
A shopper who knows exactly what they want

probes.question: True or false: when people have a clear preference, the number of options has little impact on their satisfaction.

claims.claim: Many similar options: each must be weighed against the others
claims.quote: Having too many approximately equally good options is mentally draining because each option must be weighed against alternatives to select the best one.
The satisfaction of choices by number of options available can be described by an inverted U model.

claims.claim: It rises, peaks, then falls into pressure and confusion
claims.quote: as the number of choices increases it then peaks and people tend to feel more pressure, confusion, and potentially dissatisfaction with their choice

claims.claim: Too many options can leave people less satisfied (smaller sets lead to more satisfaction)
claims.quote: smaller choice sets lead to increased satisfaction and reduced regret

claims.claim: The effect is not universal; it has preconditions
claims.quote: Choice overload is not a problem in all cases, there are some preconditions that must be met before the effect can take place.

claims.claim: Needs a chooser with no clear prior preference (probe 1)
claims.quote: people making the choice must not have a clear prior preference for an item type or category
there must not be a clearly dominant option in the choice set

claims.claim: With a preference, the number of options has little impact on satisfaction (probe 2)
claims.quote: When the choice-maker has a preference, the number of options has little impact on the final decision and satisfaction.
